nodes.label: BizzAR — WebAR SaaS Product
nodes.rationale: Turns physical business cards into interactive AR experiences. Pure WebAR (no app install). Individual professionals as primary target. QR+Image Tracking delivery model.

nodes.label: Standalone AR Viewer (no React)
nodes.rationale: AR viewer at /ar/[userId]/[cardId] is standalone HTML with no React shell. 8th Wall + A-Frame loaded via script tags. Rationale: AR runtimes conflict with React DOM reconciliation; bundle must be tiny for fast mobile load.

nodes.label: Two Separate Rendering Environments
nodes.rationale: Editor uses React+R3F; AR viewer is standalone HTML. These must never be mixed. Standalone AR viewer is non-negotiable for performance and AR runtime compatibility.

nodes.label: 3D Hub Editor (R3F Isometric View)
nodes.rationale: Orthographic camera at isometric angle. OrbitControls via Drei. 4 panel planes at fixed PANEL_TRANSFORMS. Use eventSource+eventPrefix on Canvas + pointer-events:none CSS to avoid Html overlay blocking R3F raycasting.

nodes.label: 4×4 Magnetic Panel Grid Module System
nodes.rationale: 4-column × 4-row grid. Modules snap on drop, no overlap, bounce-back on collision. Preset size variants only (no free resize). Rationale: predictable layouts translate cleanly into 3D AR space; free resize causes layout chaos.

nodes.label: Panel Slot Layout (overlay/top/left/right)
nodes.rationale: 4 slots: overlay (on card surface), top (Nintendo DS-style 45° tilt), left/right (wing panels). Free plan gets overlay+top only. Transforms pre-calculated in PANEL_TRANSFORMS constants shared between editor and AR viewer.

nodes.label: Freemium Gate (Server-side RLS)
nodes.rationale: users.plan is the single source of truth. Gate enforced via Supabase RLS, never client-side only. Free: overlay+top panels, vCard/Socials/Bio modules, 1 card, watermark. Pro: all 4 panels, all modules, unlimited cards.

nodes.label: 8th Wall OSS / MindAR Image Tracking
nodes.rationale: 8th Wall transitioned to open source Feb 2026 (MIT for Image Targets). MindAR.js used as replacement after 8th Wall cloud SDK was removed. Image tracking: camera detects physical business card, anchors AR content to it.

nodes.label: .mind File (Compiled Image Target)
nodes.rationale: Binary file compiled by 8th Wall image-target-cli or MindAR Compiler from card image. Contains multi-scale feature descriptors for AR tracking. Stored in Supabase Storage. URL stored in cards.image_target_url.

nodes.label: Supabase Data Model (users/cards/panels/modules)
nodes.rationale: 4 tables: users (extends auth.users), cards (root entity), panels (4 auto-created per card via trigger), modules (drag-dropped onto panels). RLS on all tables. Public read only when cards.published=true.

nodes.label: Stripe Webhook Plan Upgrade Flow
nodes.rationale: checkout.session.completed → set users.plan='pro' → enable left/right panels → Supabase Realtime notifies open editor → panels unlock in real time without page reload.

nodes.label: One Euro Filter Algorithm
nodes.author: Casiez, Roussel, Vogel (CHI 2012)
nodes.rationale: Speed-adaptive low-pass filter for noisy real-time signals. Two knobs: min_cutoff (stationary smoothing) and beta (speed coefficient). Insight: people are sensitive to jitter when slow but sensitive to lag when moving fast. Used inside MindAR for pose smoothing.

nodes.label: MindAR Tracking Parameter Tuning
nodes.rationale: filterMinCF maps to One Euro min_cutoff; filterBeta maps to beta. Defaults (0.001/1000) tuned for generic demo, suboptimal for static business card. Recommended BizzAR baseline: filterMinCF:0.0001, filterBeta:5000, warmupTolerance:2, missTolerance:25.

nodes.label: SLAM vs Image Tracking Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: SLAM = world-relative persistent anchor; image tracking = target-relative, lost when card leaves frame. MindAR has no SLAM. For BizzAR v1: accept limitation, mitigate with high missTolerance + IMU fusion. V2 path: WebXR hit-test+anchors on Android, MindAR fallback on iOS.

nodes.label: AR Target Image Quality
nodes.rationale: Target quality dominates tracking stability. Requires: ≥1000px shortest side, even feature distribution across all 4 quadrants, high luminance contrast (not color contrast), no repetitive/symmetrical patterns, >300 features in compiled .mind. Wordmark-only cards are worst possible targets.

nodes.label: Mobile WebAR GPU Contention
nodes.rationale: Camera texture upload + TF.js detect/track + R3F render all compete on same GPU. Mid-tier phone budget: 21-34ms per frame → 30fps achievable, 60fps not. Mitigations: cap at 30fps, 1280×720 camera, WebGL backend, pre-warm WASM, visibilitychange teardown.

nodes.label: WebXR Image Tracking Viability (2026)
nodes.rationale: Not viable as primary tracker: iOS Safari has no WebXR support (no timeline), Chrome Android image tracking module is intermittent. For production BizzAR: MindAR for image identification, WebXR hit-test+anchors as optional Android upgrade path for persistent world tracking.

nodes.label: react-three-mind R3F Wrapper
nodes.rationale: Thin R3F wrapper over MindAR Three.js variant. Exposes ARView, ARAnchor, ARFaceMesh. Lightly maintained (v0.3.0). Known issue: bundles duplicate Three.js from MindAR. Performance issue: both loops compete for same RAF/GPU. Plan to fork for production BizzAR.

nodes.label: MindAR Internal Tracking Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Per-frame: camera frame → detectorTF (ORB-like feature extraction) → matcher (vs .mind features) → estimator (RANSAC+PnP) → trackingTF (inter-frame, cheaper) → OneEuroFilter → Object3D matrix. Detection mode (slow) vs tracking mode (fast, 5-10× cheaper). TF.js WebGL backend (custom shader ops).

nodes.label: MindAR Compiler (Browser WASM)
nodes.rationale: Compiler class runs in-browser via WASM-backed TF.js. Takes images, outputs .mind blob. Multi-scale image pyramid. Can be called client-side at card-creation time for instant feedback and feature heatmap display. No server compilation needed.

nodes.label: Path-Based Publish URLs (not subdomains)
nodes.rationale: AR viewer URL: bizzar.app/ar/[userId]/[cardId]. Rationale: subdomains require wildcard DNS + SSL cert management. Path routing is free, instant, simpler at MVP. Vanity subdomain is a future Pro feature.

nodes.label: drei Html + Orthographic Camera Fix
nodes.rationale: Do NOT use distanceFactor on drei Html with orthographic cameras — causes runaway scaling. Fix: omit distanceFactor. Also: Html overlays block R3F raycasting — fix with eventSource+eventPrefix on Canvas + pointer-events:none CSS on Html wrappers.

nodes.label: MindAR Replacing 8th Wall
nodes.rationale: 8th Wall cloud SDK is paid (free tier removed). Replaced with MindAR.js (free, open source). No API key needed. Rewrote ARScene, ARPageClient. Also: MindAR CLI fails on Node 24 — workaround is browser-based compiler.html at localhost:3002.

nodes.label: MindARThree IIFE Bundle Constructor Fix
nodes.rationale: mind-ar-three.prod.js is a webpack IIFE bundle assigning to window.MINDAR.IMAGE.MindARThree — has NO ES module exports. Destructuring {MindARThree} from dynamic import always yields undefined. Fix: await import(...) then read window.MINDAR?.IMAGE?.MindARThree.

nodes.label: Supabase Free Tier Auto-Pause
nodes.rationale: Supabase project wyujyqrblovrmnymfmms auto-pauses on free tier after inactivity. Fix: restore_project via Supabase MCP tool. Wait ~3min for ACTIVE_HEALTHY. Recurring issue.

nodes.label: Three.js Version Conflict (MindAR vs Drei)
nodes.rationale: drei v9.105 requires three>=0.155; MindAR 1.2.5 requires three<=0.151. Fix in bizzar-proto: downgrade to three@0.150.1 + drei@9.88.0. Residual 'Multiple instances of Three.js' warning is harmless. Matches react-three-mind issue #104.

nodes.label: getUserMedia Camera Constraints for WebAR
nodes.rationale: Recommended: 1280×720, 30fps cap, facingMode environment, focusMode continuous. Rationale: 1280×720 is sweet spot for feature detection vs GPU cost. 30fps aligns with camera native rate, saves ~40% heat. Continuous autofocus prevents blur-induced tracking loss.

nodes.label: Trackability Score for Card Upload Validation
nodes.rationale: Run MindAR Compiler client-side on upload, show feature heatmap, compute trackability score = feature_count × (1 − Gini_coefficient). Block save if score < threshold. Prevents bad tracking UX from ever shipping. Single highest-impact preventive measure.
nodes.norm_label: trackability score for card upload validation

nodes.label: Open Source Contribution Opportunities
nodes.rationale: Flagged per CLAUDE.md: 1) Decouple Three.js from MindAR (issue #104 open since 2022). 2) Expose controller internals via wrappers. 3) WebGPU backend port. 4) MindAR→WebXR anchor handoff library (fills 8th Wall replacement gap). 5) react-three-mind frameloop='demand' support.

nodes.label: WebAR Hybrid Tracking Strategy (2026)
nodes.rationale: MindAR for iOS + Android initial identification/anchor. WebXR hit-test+anchors on Android Chrome for persistent world tracking after initial scan. 8th Wall OSS SLAM binary as future moat option (binary-only license, self-hosting required).

nodes.label: frameloop='always' for AR
nodes.rationale: MindAR mutates Three.js matrixWorld imperatively each frame outside React. frameloop='demand' only re-renders on React state changes so the canvas would freeze with stale transforms. 'always' is mandatory for AR.

nodes.label: DPR Cap [1, 1.5] for Mobile AR
nodes.rationale: Single biggest mobile performance win. Pixel 7 Pro has 3x DPR; without cap renders 9x more pixels. At 1.5 cap renders ~2.25x pixels — 60% faster than native 3x with acceptable quality.

nodes.label: Geometry Hoisting Outside Components
nodes.rationale: Creating geometry inside React components recreates it on every render. Hoisting geometry constants outside the component scope ensures they are created once and reused.

nodes.label: Per-Module Suspense Placement
nodes.rationale: Suspense at ARContent root blanks entire canvas during async load. Per-module Suspense allows some panels (CardFrame) to render immediately while others (ContactCard) load asynchronously.

nodes.label: useFrame Priority System
nodes.rationale: MindAR updates happen at priority -1 internally. Custom useFrame callbacks should run at priority 1+ to ensure they execute AFTER MindAR pose updates are applied.

nodes.label: drei Html transform vs screen-space
nodes.rationale: transform mode scales HTML element with 3D perspective. distanceFactor must NOT be used with orthographic cameras — causes massive scaling. BizzAR has moved to native R3F meshes, avoiding Html entirely.

nodes.label: SDF Font Rendering via drei Text
nodes.rationale: Troika-three-text renders SDF in a Web Worker without blocking the main thread. Better than canvas-texture text for sharp rendering at any DPR on mobile AR.
nodes.norm_label: sdf font rendering via drei text

nodes.label: SLAM vs Image Tracking Algorithm Difference
nodes.rationale: Image tracking (MindAR) requires target in frame at all times, no memory between frames. SLAM builds a 3D map and localizes within it, enabling AR panels to persist even when card is occluded. SLAM requires significantly more compute.
nodes.norm_label: slam vs image tracking algorithm difference

nodes.label: 8th Wall Shutdown and OSS Transition
nodes.rationale: 8th Wall shut down Feb 28 2026 after Niantic acquisition. Transitioned to open source at 8thwall.org. Image Targets and face/world effects are MIT, but the SLAM engine binary has commercial restrictions. Post-Niantic community support uncertain.

nodes.label: WebXR iOS Support Gap
nodes.rationale: Safari iOS has zero WebXR support with no announced timeline. iOS represents 50%+ of users. Cannot rely on WebXR image tracking or SLAM as primary approach — MindAR (non-WebXR) is required for cross-platform.

nodes.label: BizzAR WebAR Stack Decision 2026
nodes.rationale: MindAR+react-three-mind+R3F+drei+Three.js is the correct free stack in 2026. No credible free alternative exists. 8th Wall shutdown created power vacuum; MindAR fills free/OSS space. Zappar requires paid ZapWorks subscription.

nodes.label: MeshBasicMaterial for AR Panels
nodes.rationale: AR overlay panels are flat and don't need lighting. MeshBasicMaterial has zero lighting calculations — cheapest option. MeshStandardMaterial (PBR) is expensive on mobile. Only use MeshStandardMaterial for 3D model modules.

nodes.label: COOP/COEP Headers Scoped to AR Route
nodes.rationale: SharedArrayBuffer for WASM threading requires COOP/COEP headers. Applying globally breaks Stripe Payment Element, Google OAuth popups, and third-party iframes. Must be scoped to /ar/* only.
nodes.norm_label: coop/coep headers scoped to ar route

nodes.label: facingMode ideal vs exact
nodes.rationale: Using exact facingMode throws OverconstrainedError on devices with only one camera (some tablets). 'ideal' falls back gracefully. Always use ideal not exact for robust cross-device compatibility.

nodes.label: 1280x720 Sweet Spot for MindAR
nodes.rationale: 640x480 gives too few features. 1920x1080 is wasted since MindAR downsamples internally with 720p as effective quality ceiling. 1280x720 is the sweet spot — good feature detection with moderate performance cost.

nodes.label: In-App Browser Detection for AR
nodes.rationale: WKWebView in Instagram, TikTok, Telegram blocks camera access entirely. Critical for BizzAR since cards are shared via social apps. Must detect and show 'Open in Safari/Chrome' banner.

nodes.label: .mind File Format
nodes.rationale: Binary msgpack format prefixed with version byte (v2). Contains matchingData (KPM keypoints with BRIEF descriptors) and trackingData (lighter point set). Raw pixel data NOT stored, keeping files 50-200KB per target.

nodes.label: MindAR Compiler Requires SSR False
nodes.rationale: mind-ar uses Web Workers and Canvas APIs unavailable in Node.js SSR environment. Must use dynamic import with ssr:false in Next.js to prevent server-side crash.

nodes.label: MindAR Uses TF.js as WebGL Compute Engine
nodes.rationale: MindAR is pure JS with no WASM. It uses TensorFlow.js as a WebGL abstraction to run custom GPU shaders for computer vision operations — not for machine learning. This is the key architectural insight.
nodes.norm_label: mindar uses tf.js as webgl compute engine

nodes.label: maxTrack=1 for Single Card Experience
nodes.rationale: Detection phase (expensive: feature extraction + matching) only runs on non-tracked targets. maxTrack=1 is most CPU-efficient. On mid-range mobile maxTrack=3+ will cause frame drops. BizzAR single-card model should keep maxTrack=1.

nodes.label: Luminance Contrast Over Color Contrast
nodes.rationale: Tracking engine converts to grayscale before processing. Color contrast does not help unless it translates to luminance contrast. Dark blue on black or yellow on white fail in grayscale even if vivid in color.

nodes.label: Symmetry Causes AR Tracking Orientation Flip
nodes.rationale: Centered symmetric logos cause 180 degree flip ambiguity — tracking engine cannot determine correct orientation. Bilateral symmetry causes ambiguous horizontal position. Most common mistake in business card AR design.
nodes.norm_label: symmetry causes ar tracking orientation flip

nodes.label: Feature Distribution Across Image Quadrants
nodes.rationale: Homography estimation requires 4+ non-collinear matches. Features clustered in center leave card corners unconstrained causing perspective wobble. Features must span all four quadrants for stable pose estimation.

nodes.label: SSR False Dynamic Import for AR Bundle
nodes.rationale: Three.js, MindAR, react-three-mind access window/document/navigator/WebGL at import time. Node.js SSR has none of these. Dynamic import with ssr:false prevents crash and also keeps the 2MB AR bundle out of main app bundle.
nodes.norm_label: ssr false dynamic import for ar bundle

nodes.label: AR Vendor Bundle Splitting via Webpack
nodes.rationale: three, @react-three, react-three-mind, mind-ar total ~2MB gzipped. Splitting into a separate async chunk ensures this is only loaded when user navigates to /ar/* route, keeping main app bundle fast.
nodes.norm_label: ar vendor bundle splitting via webpack

nodes.label: Service Worker Caching for .mind Files
nodes.rationale: .mind files are ~500KB and rarely change. Aggressive service worker caching means returning users skip the network fetch entirely — critical for fast AR startup on second scan.

nodes.label: Add to Contacts as Primary AR Conversion Action
nodes.rationale: ~80% of users who scan a card just want to save the contact. Only ~20% explore additional panels. Add to Contacts is the #1 conversion action and must be prominent and instant.
nodes.norm_label: add to contacts as primary ar conversion action

nodes.label: AR Differentiation Gap in Business Card Market
nodes.rationale: None of the major digital card platforms (Popl, HiHello, Linq, dot.cards) do real AR. 8th Wall shutdown fragmented the polished commercial WebAR market. BizzAR has a clear differentiation opportunity.
nodes.norm_label: ar differentiation gap in business card market

nodes.label: Sparkles on Card Detection Wow Moment
nodes.rationale: GPU-instanced particles via drei Sparkles = 1 draw call for 35 particles. Highest wow-per-line-of-code ratio (~5 lines). Triggers on isTracking state. BizzAR brand color #818cf8 indigo.
nodes.norm_label: sparkles on card detection wow moment

nodes.label: Spring Physics Panel Entrance Animation
nodes.rationale: @react-spring/three animated.group with scale 0→1 on card detection. Staggered delays (frame:0ms, contact:100ms, socials:250ms, github:400ms) create polished reveal sequence. config.wobbly gives bouncy pop feel.

nodes.label: react-three-mind Library
nodes.rationale: Thin wrapper (500 lines) wrapping MindAR inside R3F Canvas+frame loop. Ships its own Three.js copy causing potential version conflicts. Not all MindAR controller options forwarded. Single maintainer (tommasoturchi). Fork opportunity for BizzAR.

nodes.label: AlvaAR GPL License Blocker
nodes.rationale: AlvaAR is ORB-SLAM2 compiled to WASM but licensed GPLv3 — incompatible with commercial SaaS without open-sourcing the entire codebase or purchasing a commercial license. Not viable for BizzAR.

nodes.label: model-viewer AR Quick Look iOS Fallback
nodes.rationale: For iOS users where WebAR detection fails or camera is denied, a model-viewer component with USDZ asset provides native AR Quick Look without requiring WebXR. Strong iOS fallback strategy.
nodes.norm_label: model-viewer ar quick look ios fallback

nodes.label: Pictarize Three-Dimension Trackability Score
nodes.rationale: Distribution (even feature spread across regions), Uniqueness (descriptors distinguishable from each other), Resolution (>1000px per dimension). BizzAR should compute all three from dataList returned by compileImageTargets.

nodes.label: MindAR dummyRun Pre-warming GPU Kernels
nodes.rationale: Calling controller.dummyRun() before the first real frame pre-warms WebGL shader compilation, preventing 500-1500ms jank on the initial detection frame. Should be called after addImageTargets.

nodes.label: KTX2/Basis Universal Texture Compression
nodes.rationale: Reduces GPU memory 4-6x vs PNG/JPEG for runtime textures. Requires WASM + SharedArrayBuffer (COOP/COEP headers). Viable for v2+ after user-uploaded card photos are a bottleneck, not needed for v1 single texture.
